record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; source code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports behavioral results for models produced with a weight-edit implementation of directional ablation, rather than the original activation-projection intervention.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal and PPL outcomes for exported Heretic models. Its geometry example and descriptions of parameters are not additional outcome rows. The comparison rows for other abliterated Gemma models are not included because the README does not report that this repository produced or tested them.
record.test_reason: The fork's own README reports refusal and perplexity for two Ministral-3-3B models edited by weight-level directional ablation. The direction is a difference-of-means, optimized over layers and components. Refusal falls from 47/136 to 2/136 and 7/136 with negligible PPL change. This bears on V2 directly and on V1's ablation and capability parts.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The fork presents Heretic-MOE as a reproducible, architecture-aware extension of Heretic's directional ablation. Its own evidence is one frozen Ministral-3-3B evaluation: policy refusal drops sharply with negligible PPL change. The README states this is 'not a claim of universal behavior'. The Gemma-3-12b comparison is upstream Heretic's result, not the fork's.
record.recipe_differences: This is a fork of Heretic that retains directional ablation but edits component weight matrices, uses configurable/interpolated residual directions and optimized layer/component parameters, and adds search and export workflows. The README describes difference-of-means residual directions from first-token harmful and harmless prompts.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says ablation weights are optimized separately by component and can vary over layers; the reference workflow uses different selection rules for Balanced and Max.
record.problems: Evidence is reported in the README without uncertainty estimates. The capability-related evidence is limited to KL divergence and PPL proxies; the README itself cautions that automated metrics do not tell the whole story. The repository code was not read or run.
record.rows_left_out: The README's delivered, evasion, and refusal-plus-evasion counts in the Ministral table were left out because they are not the direct policy-refusal measure named by these claim versions. Comparison values for other Gemma abliterations were left out because the README does not report that this repository produced or tested those models.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; activation-level ablation at all layers and positions; a single fixed direction (the fork interpolates and optimizes directions and per-layer weights); task-level capability benchmarks.
Only one fork-produced model family (Ministral-3-3B) has reported results here; the other released Heretic models are asserted, not measured in this text.

record.verdict_notes: The source is a README, so there are no uncertainty estimates and the code was not inspected. The rows_left_out field declares the delivered, evasion and refusal-plus-evasion counts. They matter for V2, because a large share of responses still evade after editing; researchers may want them added as rows. Finalists were chosen by search-time proxies and then validated by a separate blind semantic pass, so selection effects are possible but limited. The listed configs for Gemma2, Gemma4, Qwen3-VL-32B and Qwen3.6 report no results in this text.

versions.untested_parts: The README reports refusal outcomes for weight-edited models, but does not test adding the direction to induce harmless-request refusals or the exact activation ablation at every layer and position. PPL and KL are proxies, not a broad general-capability evaluation.
Results are reported for the named model variants and frozen evaluations, not for released models generally.

relationships.condition: Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512, max and balanced weight-edited exports, 136-prompt frozen blind semantic evaluation
relationships.reason: Policy refusal falls from 47/136 to 2/136 (max, r3) and 7/136 (balanced, r4) in the released weight-edited models.
relationships.display_finding: Policy refusals fell from 47/136 to 2/136 for the max edit and 7/136 for the balanced edit.

relationships.condition: Same Ministral exports, counting evasion as well as refusal
relationships.reason: From the README table: evasion stays at 32/136 (max) and 42/136 (balanced), so only 101/136 and 85/136 are delivered. Removal depends on which export is chosen (r3, r4).
relationships.display_finding: The max export evaded 32/136 prompts and delivered 101/136 answers, while the balanced export evaded 42/136 and delivered 85/136.

relationships.condition: Ministral-3-3B, ablation of a difference-of-means direction applied as a weight edit
relationships.reason: Refusal is nearly removed (r3, r4) while exact PPL changes by under 0.05% (r5, r6).
relationships.display_finding: Refusal was nearly eliminated while exact perplexity changed by less than 0.05%.
